expectations_used.clarify: Pins down what the partition guard is actually meant to cover — asks whether it protects only the partition's entry map, LRU order and byte accounting or is also meant to single-flight concurrent reads of the same key, and whether two threads hydrating different shards of one dataset are supposed to overlap — instead of assuming `docs/hydrator.md` settles it.
expectations_used.approach: States a mechanism before editing — e.g. that `_hydrate_one` takes the per-dataset partition guard and still holds it while `_load_with_retry` calls the loader, so three shards of `orbital_passes` serialize behind one lock and never reach the barrier together — rather than 'a threading problem' or 'something in the pool'.
expectations_used.communicate: Keeps a running account of the hunt rather than reporting only conclusions: names each file opened and why, reads the `BrokenBarrierError` and the 2-second runtime out loud as evidence that the loaders never overlapped, and says which suspects (the `AdmissionGate` condition variable, `min(max_workers, len(specs))`, the retry `time.sleep`, `as_completed`) are being ruled out and on what basis — so a listener could retrace the path without having to interrupt and ask what is being tried.
expectations_used.implement: Narrows the critical section so the store read happens outside the partition guard — re-taking the guard only to check for a concurrent insert and `put` the payload — while leaving `_require_guard` satisfied, `MISSING`/`FAILED` outcome handling intact, and the pool, gate, retry and dedupe code untouched.
expectations_used.verify: Re-runs `python3 -m unittest discover -v`, confirms `test_shards_of_one_dataset_hydrate_concurrently` passes and all 15 tests are green, notices the suite now finishes in milliseconds instead of two seconds, and checks a case the suite does not cover — e.g. that a shard failing mid-dataset still leaves the partition writable and `inflight_bytes` at zero.
expectations_used.reflect: Explains why the bug hid: the cross-dataset overlap test passes because each dataset has its own guard, so nothing in the suite except one same-dataset case ever contends, and the visible symptom is a barrier timeout in a fixture rather than an error in the hydrator — and names what would surface it earlier, such as asserting on observed overlap per dataset or on loader concurrency.

summary: The candidate eventually landed on a fix that turned the suite green and matched the actual root cause (the partition guard held across the retried load serializing same-dataset shard reads), but the path there was almost entirely interviewer-driven through repeated nudges, with long unfocused stretches of print-statement debugging, syntax questions misdirected at the interviewer, and visible frustration. Self-directed hypothesis formation, narration, and root-cause explanation were all weak, with verification being the only dimension meeting a baseline bar.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate never asked a targeted question resolving what the partition guard was meant to cover, nor what the barrier-based test was actually asserting about concurrency until the interviewer forced the point repeatedly starting around the 800s mark. Instead of clarifying the mechanism up front, they spent long stretches asking the interviewer to validate Python syntax (dict comprehensions, future-as-key) rather than resolving the actual ambiguity about what the test expected.

No mechanism was proposed before editing; the candidate largely floundered with print-statement debugging without a stated hypothesis, and only converged on 'we weren't locking' after heavy interviewer nudging past the 900s and 1400s marks. Even the eventual framing was vague ('there was a lot of concurrency there I guess') rather than naming holding the guard across the retried load as the mechanism before editing.

Long stretches of unfilled pauses, trailing sentences, and repeated syntax questions dominate the transcript; the interviewer had to repeatedly stop and re-focus the candidate rather than the candidate narrating a coherent investigative thread. Multiple silent/transcription-gap periods coincide with edits, and even where speech is present it rarely states what is being ruled in or out.

Implementation consisted of scattered print-statement additions and edits with no clear connection to a stated theory, many edited/saved cycles without narrated purpose, and the eventual correct-looking fix around 1868s arrived only after extensive nudged narrowing rather than a scoped, deliberate change.

The candidate did re-run the test suite after the final edit and confirmed all tests passed, and the interviewer additionally pointed out the runtime drop from two seconds to milliseconds, which the candidate did not proactively check but did not contradict either. There was no additional edge-case check (e.g., partition state after a failed shard) initiated by the candidate.

When asked to explain the mechanism, the candidate could only vaguely gesture at 'not locking' and later, after correction, described holding the lock across retry but could not explain why only one test caught it, admitting outright they had no clue when pressed on this at the end.
